picks.catalyst: Earnings beat + raised full-year sales forecast
picks.why: Palo Alto beat estimates (revenue up 39% to $3.44B) and raised its yearly sales forecast, and it's up about 9-10% before the open; a big, well-known company beating and raising is the classic setup that can keep moving all day. Reports differ between +9% and +10%, so use the live quote for price.

picks.catalyst: Earnings beat + raised guidance (3rd straight raise)
picks.why: Everpure (the old Pure Storage) grew sales 51%, beat profit estimates, and raised its yearly forecast for the third quarter in a row, so it jumped about 6% after hours from a $100.74 close; the stock had fallen ~29% in the past month, so good news can spark a strong bounce. The +6% is the after-hours move, not a fresh pre-market quote - check it.

picks.catalyst: First outside customer for its newest 18A chip-making process
picks.why: Intel's CEO said it signed its first outside customer for its most advanced chip factory process (the customer wasn't named), which is a big step for its factory business, and the stock is up about 4% from a $54.67 close; it also fell 12% in the past five days, so it has room to bounce. Because the customer is unnamed, the move could fade if no details come out.

picks.catalyst: Sympathy move: Palo Alto beat-and-raise lifts cybersecurity
picks.why: CrowdStrike has no news of its own today; it's up about 5-7% because its biggest rival Palo Alto posted strong results, which makes investors more upbeat about the whole security group. Sympathy moves follow the leader, so if PANW fades, CRWD likely fades too.

picks.catalyst: Owns a big stake in Anthropic, which prices a record IPO today
picks.why: Alphabet is up about 4% because it owns roughly 1.8 billion shares of Anthropic, whose record IPO priced at $83 (above the expected range) and starts trading today; the move depends on how Anthropic trades, so expect swings once it opens.

avoid.why: Stock offering: sold $150M of new shares at $13 the day after a big trial-data spike (down ~18-21% pre-market) - dilution
Anthropic's first trading day (IPO priced at $83) - no trading history and huge first-day swings, too wild for a beginner
